dims.flowdec: F = source window (f0, phase, noise_offsets; S = F * upp); Fz = F - latent_offset = flow_margin + main_margin + R = latent window (m_p, logs_p, z_noise: the text encoder's output is needed over these frames only); A = (F - flow_margin - dec_margin) * upp; f0 frames before flow_margin - 1, phase / src_noise frames before flow_margin and noise_offsets before flow_margin + latent_offset are not read
dims.knn: T = 20 ms content frames; N >= min_index_rows

phase.value: phase[j] = frac(phase0 + sum(wrap(upp * f0 / sr)) over the earlier frames), per window frame, computed in f64; wrap(x) = fmod(x + 0.5, 1) - 0.5 (the same carry as the HiFi-GAN templates' phase0, at every window frame)

excitation.linear_note: Applio's half-pixel linear f0 interpolation is computed in the graph in closed form; window frame flow_margin - 1 is its left context. Its second half-frame reads the next frame's f0, so the window's last frame is edge-clamped: with no lookahead, the phase at the end of a tick's last frame differs from the next tick's phase at that boundary by upp / (8 sr) * (f0[j+1] - f0[j]) cycles (up to ~0.2 cycle at a voicing offset). Decoding f0_lookahead_frames more frames than are returned (drop them, or delay the output by that much) keeps the excitation phase-continuous across ticks

adain.offsets: noise_offsets[0, j] = any fixed function of window frame j's absolute frame index, in [0, pool.count - per_frame]; equal inputs for equal absolute frames make overlapping ticks identical

pool.fill: iid standard normal values, generated once by the engine (any generator)

adain.element: layer (stage, layer), channel c, frame j, sample s -> pool[noise_offsets[j] + base + c * rate + s]
